html:
If you live in Greer ZIP 29650 and the last professional clean was months ago, a deep cleaning is the place to start. It is the visit that handles what routine cleaning skips: grout, cabinet fronts, baseboards, vents and the range hood. This page explains what is in it, in what order the team works, and how to decide whether you need one now or a regular clean will do.

ZIP 29650 is one of three ZIP codes for Greer, along with 29651 and 29652. Greer sits in Greenville and Spartanburg counties, with I-85, SC-14, SC-101 and US-29 running through it. Our team is based here, which means short drives and a good sense of the homes: historic houses near Downtown Greer and Trade Street, and newer neighborhoods near GSP Airport and the BMW plant.

Regular clean or deep clean?

A regular visit keeps a home level: floors, surfaces, bathrooms, kitchen. A deep clean goes into the layers. If you can run a finger along the baseboard and see a gray line, or if grout in the shower has darkened, the house needs a deep clean first. Here is a quick check.

You noticeLikely need
Dust on baseboards and fan bladesDeep cleaning
Grease on cabinet fronts near the stoveDeep cleaning
Home was cleaned recently, only needs upkeepRegular house cleaning
Moving out of the houseMove-out cleaning

What the team covers

  • Everything in a regular house cleaning.
  • Baseboards and door frames hand-wiped.
  • Cabinet fronts and handles degreased.
  • Grout lines scrubbed in kitchen and bathrooms.
  • Ceiling fan blades, vents and light fixtures dusted.
  • Window sills, tracks and blinds cleaned.
  • Behind and around the toilet base.
  • Appliance exteriors, range hood and backsplash.

Our deep cleaning in Greer page has the full list, and the deep cleaning service page explains how it differs from a standard visit.

The order of work

The team starts with the kitchen, since grease needs time to soften. While degreaser sits on the stovetop and hood, someone starts the bathrooms. Fans, vents and fixtures are dusted from above, then baseboards and door frames, then bedrooms and living rooms. Floors are the last step in each room.

Walking the house at the end, with the room list in hand, is part of the method. Small misses, such as a switch plate or a corner under a chair, are fixed before the team leaves.

How much does deep cleaning cost in Greer ZIP 29650?

We do not quote prices without seeing the home. A free in-home estimate is how we price: the team visits, sees the rooms and condition, and gives you the number, with no commitment. Because every house differs, a price from a photo would be a guess.

  • Home size: square feet and number of rooms set the base time.
  • Condition: heavy build-up takes longer to remove.
  • Add-ons: inside the oven, fridge or cabinets adds time.
  • Bathrooms: grout and hard water spots are the slowest work.
  • Access: clutter-free rooms clean faster.

Book on the Greer booking form, call (864) 399-5168 or text (864) 666-8520.

How long it takes

Most homes take a team several hours to a full day, depending on size and condition. A home that has gone a year without a professional visit takes longer than one cleaned in the spring. We usually can schedule the visit within the week after the estimate, although busy periods before holidays fill up.

How to prepare

  • Pick up toys, clothes and papers so surfaces are reachable.
  • Tell us about pets and where they will stay.
  • Decide whether you want the inside of the oven or fridge done.
  • Note spots to focus on, like a shower with heavy build-up.

What deep cleaning does not include

It is worth being clear about the limits. A deep clean is not a repair or a restoration. We do not remove permanent stains, refinish floors, or take apart appliances. Exterior pressure washing is a different job and not something we do. Carpets are vacuumed thoroughly, but shampooing is separate. If you need any of these, tell us at the estimate and we will say honestly what we can and cannot do.

Common reasons Greer homeowners book it

  • Moving into a house that was previously rented or empty.
  • Getting the home ready before starting recurring maid service.
  • Preparing for visitors or a family event.
  • A change in life, such as a new baby or an illness, after which the cleaning slipped.
  • Listing the home for sale and wanting it to show well.

In each case the goal is the same: remove built-up dirt once, so ongoing visits only maintain it. When a deep clean is skipped and regular visits start on a neglected house, the first few visits spend their time catching up.

A short note on method

Perfect Services is a Brazilian-owned team, and our detail-first method means corners, edges and small items are done by hand rather than with a quick spray. In a deep clean, that approach shows most: the baseboard line is clean to the wall, the grout is lighter, and handles and switches are wiped. If you want to understand it better, our page on Brazilian house cleaning explains the details.

What happens after

People who book a deep clean often continue with recurring visits, because a baseline is easier to maintain than to rebuild. Families in nearby places, such as Duncan, follow the same pattern. For hosts preparing for guests, our holiday deep cleaning guide covers the timing in more detail.

When you are ready, send the details through the estimate form. A few lines about your house and the last time it was cleaned is enough to start.
